DT-27 (2026-11-19): the design-system gallery had zero consumers - the activity that hosted it was deleted in the round-1 cleanup - so it was shipping dead UI in release builds while its fixtures still documented this task. It moved to src/debug instead of being deleted (evidence preserved) or left in main (release bloat); ShomaraCatalogMatrix stays in src/main because ShomaraCatalogMatrixTest asserts it. Structural proof from the class outputs: compileReleaseKotlin emits only ShomaraCatalogMatrix.class, while compileDebugKotlin also emits ShomaraCatalogGalleryKt.class and ComposableSingletons$ShomaraCatalogGalleryKt.class. :core:designsystem compiles on both variants and its JVM tests pass.

DT-33 (2026-11-19): AGENTS §6 asks for 360/390/412dp widths AND text zoom, but the sweep had only ever rendered at the device's own width and 1.0x. The shared helper assertFitsAtNarrowWidth now renders six routed pages at 360dp with fontScale 2.0 (the binding extreme) and checks both the a11y contract and text overflow. The first overflow check was USELESS and was replaced rather than kept: bounds stay inside the viewport because Compose clips, so nothing ever failed. Reading TextLayoutResult.hasVisualOverflow instead exposed a real defect — 37 text nodes are clipped at 2x (Home 8, Settings 11, Me 7, PracticeHub 7, OnboardingProfile 2, ParentHome 2), which hits exactly the users who rely on system font scaling. The mechanism was measured, not guessed: every clipped node reported didWidth=true, didHeight=false, lines=1 with layout.size == node.size, i.e. fixed-WIDTH containers too narrow at 2x for even one word (there is no maxLines anywhere in feature/path). Because a structural reflow of the path is a larger change than this round should risk, the check ships as a measured per-screen RATCHET that may only go down, with all 37 labels named in the KDoc. It was proven non-vacuous by tightening Home's budget from 8 to 7 and watching the test fail, then restoring it. Sweep is at 39 cases.

DT-34 (2026-11-19) RETRACTION of DT-33: the clipping instrument was itself broken. While trying to FIX the 37 "clipped" labels, three hypotheses were tested with data. (1) Fixed container width: making the Settings avatar grid two columns at large font made the count WORSE (11 -> 12), so the hypothesis was rejected and the change reverted. (2) A lineHeight that does not scale: the tokens are sp-based (30/26/20) and do scale, rejected. (3) The instrument: a calibration test rendered one Caption squeezed into a 24dp box and the same caption unconstrained — TextLayoutResult.hasVisualOverflow reported TRUE for BOTH, so in this Compose version that flag is not a clipping oracle. Consequence: DT-33's 37-node register was a false positive and was WITHDRAWN, not patched — the CLIPPED_TEXT_BUDGET ratchet and its per-label table are gone, the bounds check (weak but sound) is back, and the calibration test is kept as hasVisualOverflowIsNotAClippingOracle so nobody rebuilds an a11y assertion on that flag. Both experimental production changes (ShomaraPathChapter badge, ShomaraSettingsScreen grid) were reverted because neither proved an effect. Lesson recorded: a new assertion must be CALIBRATED (shown to report both true and false on controlled inputs); proving only that it can fail is not enough. The 2x text-clipping question is open again and needs a trustworthy instrument. Sweep is at 40 cases.

DT-35 (2026-11-19): the clipping question DT-34 left open was closed with a CALIBRATED oracle instead of another flag. textThatCannotFit does not ask Compose whether something overflowed; it reads the text, style and the exact constraints the real layout got (input data, not a verdict), re-measures with a real TextMeasurer, and compares the space the text NEEDS against the space it was given. It was calibrated first (textFitOracleFlagsATightBoxAndClearsAFreeLabel proves it flags a Caption squeezed into 24dp and clears the same caption left free) — the step DT-33 skipped. Run over the six routed pages at 360dp/2x with a zero budget, it found exactly ONE label that cannot fit in the whole app: the chapter digit in the path band, measured as needing 119px of height inside a 105px (40dp) fixed square. That single number, not 37, is the real finding, and it was fixed: the badge now uses defaultMinSize instead of size, so the band geometry is unchanged at 1x and the badge grows at large text. The oracle then reported 1 -> 0 and every screen keeps a budget of ZERO, which is a strictly stronger assertion than any ratchet. It also explains why the same change looked pointless in DT-34: the broken instrument could not see it. Sweep is at 41 cases.

DT-36 (2026-11-19): the calibrated 360dp/2x matrix was widened from six pages to NINE surfaces (StationSheetLocked, LessonDiscover, ParentGateLockedOut added), all at a zero text-fit budget. It immediately found a SECOND real defect of the same family as DT-35: the station sheet chapter badge is a fixed 40dp square holding a Title digit, measured as needing 119px of height in a 105px slot. So the pattern is "fixed 40dp square + Title digit", not a one-off. It was fixed the same way (defaultMinSize), and grep confirmed that was the last .size(ShomaraTokens.Space40) in any feature module, so the whole family is covered. One accessibility-tested surface could not be opened by tapping at 360dp - Compose reported "Failed to inject touch input" because the far station sits below the fold - so that case renders the sheet composable directly, which is the same thing the shell hosts, instead of pretending a click happened. Net: nine surfaces at 2x report ZERO text that cannot fit, budgets stay at zero. Sweep is at 44 cases.

DT-37 (2026-11-19): Home is now measured in all four of its entry states at 360dp/2x, not just with a resolved path: HomeLoading, HomeError, HomeEmpty and HomeOffline each have their own case against the calibrated text-fit oracle at a zero budget, and the Error case additionally pins the pairing between the canonical "try again" copy and the retry affordance so a future wiring cannot ship a message that instructs an action the screen does not offer. The first version of that test built an unresolved ShomaraPathProgress carrying station ids and the constructor rejected it ("unresolved progress cannot carry fabricated or partial station state") - the TEST was corrected, not the invariant, so the anti-fabrication rule kept its teeth; Offline is the only one of the four that legitimately carries station data. A technical limit was also learned: a Compose test can call setContent once, so the four states are four tests behind one helper rather than a loop. Separately: a windowed duplication scan over 221 hand-written files produced 687 matching groups that were almost all import blocks and KDoc, i.e. no further layout duplication worth merging - recorded as a negative so it is not chased again - and git ls-files confirmed zero tracked build/ or generated/ files with **/build/ ignored as AGENTS section 4 requires. Sweep is at 48 cases.

DT-38 (2026-11-19): `lint` is listed in AGENTS section 7 as part of the native gate but had no npm script and had never been run in this session. Running :app:lintDebug and then lint on ALL modules (app-only lint skips library modules by default) surfaced four real UI-code defects, all fixed: (1) DefaultLocale - ShomaraCharacter.labelFor used String.format("%02d") without a Locale, and that value is the asset-path key, so a locale formatting %02d with non-ASCII digits would silently lose the character artwork; now Locale.ROOT. (2) ComposableNaming - the design system exposed shomaraBackHandler in lowercase next to ShomaraTheme/ShomaraTokens; renamed to ShomaraBackHandler across five call sites (the rename itself exposed a sixth call site in feature:lesson that broke the build and was fixed in the same pass). (3) ModifierParameter - ShomaraPlacementScreen had modifier after another optional parameter; moved to the first optional slot, and since every call site uses named arguments no caller changed. (4) MonochromeLauncherIcon x2 - a monochrome layer was added to both adaptive icons for Android 13+ themed icons. A weak a11y test was strengthened too: ShomaraFontScaleTest only checked didOverflowHeight (the flag family DT-34 disproved), so it now also compares the paragraph's real measured height with its box. Result: core:designsystem 3 -> 0, feature:onboarding 1 -> 0, feature:lesson 0, app 21 -> 19 (remaining are dependency-version, manifest-attribute and screen-orientation items, not UI code). Two findings were deliberately NOT changed and are handed to the owner: the locked screen orientation (Android 16 ignores it anyway, and unlocking it needs a landscape layout review) and NotShrinkingResources (release-only effect, and a release build is neither sanctioned nor possible here, so it was not flipped unverified - getIdentifier usage is zero, so the risk is low when it is). Evidence: lint exit 0 on all modules, ShomaraA11ySweepTest 48/48, ShomaraFontScaleTest 16/16, android:gate exit 0.

DT-39 (2026-11-19): owner feedback was that the UI is not attractive, with a character-led hero chosen as the first direction. ShomaraHomeHeader was turned from a bare text row into a real card: ColorHomeVioletSoft accent surface, RadiusLg corners, Soft clay depth, the character enlarged to ComponentNodeCurrent + Space16 as the visual anchor, Title heading and a VioletDark subtitle with better contrast than Muted. Prominence deliberately came from colour and scale rather than the Featured depth tier, because depthFor(Current) is Featured and ADR-0040 allows at most one Featured surface per viewport - so the current station keeps its rank. No new copy was invented; only the existing canonical Title/Subtitle/Settings strings are used. The full sweep stayed at 48/48 including the nine 360dp/2x surfaces with the calibrated text-fit oracle, so the card neither clips text at 2x nor breaks the heading/a11y contract. Honest limit: this agent cannot read images, so a real device screenshot was captured for the owner instead of claiming the result looks good: build-reports/ui/home-default.png.

ShomaraChapterProgressCard (C04) and ShomaraContinueStationCard (C05) now render the real chapter and the real current station with exactly one primary action, and the primary-CTA claim moved off the path node via currentNodeClaimsPrimaryCta so the continue card owns it - with the node keeping it whenever no card is rendered, so Home can never end up with zero primary actions.
